subject: chemistry
topic: Atomic structure, isotopes and electron configuration

kept.q: The nucleus of an atom contains protons and neutrons, while electrons occupy the space around it. Which of the following correctly states the relative charge and mass of a proton compared to an electron?
options: A proton has the same charge magnitude as an electron but opposite sign, and is about 1836 times heavier
A proton has twice the charge of an electron and is about 1836 times heavier
A proton and electron have equal mass but opposite charges
A proton has no charge but is heavier than an electron
kept.explanation: A proton carries a +1 charge while an electron carries a -1 charge, so they are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign. A proton is about 1836 times more massive than an electron, which is why electrons are treated as negligible in mass calculations.

kept.q: Which of the following statements correctly explains why isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties?
options: They have the same number of neutrons in the nucleus
They have the same number of protons and therefore the same number of electrons and electron arrangement
They have the same mass number but different atomic numbers
They have different numbers of electrons but the same number of protons
kept.explanation: Chemical properties depend mainly on the number and arrangement of electrons, which is determined by the atomic number (number of protons). Isotopes differ only in neutron number, so their electron configuration and chemical behaviour remain the same.

kept.q: An ion is formed when a neutral atom of potassium (atomic number 19) loses one electron. Write the correct electron configuration of the resulting potassium ion.
kept.explanation: Neutral potassium has configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s1 with 19 electrons. Losing one electron from the outermost 4s orbital gives 18 electrons, matching 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6, which is the stable noble gas arrangement of argon.
kept.pidgin: Potassium get 19 electrons, but if e lose one, e go remain 18. Dat 18 electrons go arrange like 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6, wey be like noble gas.

kept.q: In the modern quantum mechanical model of the atom, which set of quantum numbers describes the azimuthal (orbital angular momentum) quantum number, l, for a 3d electron?
kept.explanation: The azimuthal quantum number l determines the subshell type: l = 0 is s, l = 1 is p, l = 2 is d and l = 3 is f. Since the electron is in a d subshell, l must equal 2.
kept.pidgin: For quantum numbers, l = 0 na s, l = 1 na p, and l = 2 na d. Since we dey talk about 3d electron, l must be 2.

kept.q: Using the Aufbau principle and electron-filling order, determine the correct ground-state electron configuration of a sulphur atom (atomic number 16).
kept.explanation: Sulphur has 16 electrons which fill up in order of increasing energy: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4, giving a total of 2+2+6+2+4 = 16. This configuration correctly follows the Aufbau filling order without exceeding orbital capacities.
kept.pidgin: Sulphur get 16 electrons, so we go arrange dem as 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p4. If you add all the numbers, e go give you 16, wey follow the correct order.

q.q: Consider a neutral atom with electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d5 4s1. This configuration is unusually stable mainly because
options: a half-filled d subshell gives extra stability due to symmetrical electron distribution
the atom has lost all its valence electrons
the 4s orbital is always lower in energy than 3d in every atom
q.explanation: A half-filled d subshell (3d5) has a symmetrical distribution of electrons which gives extra exchange stabilisation energy. This is why some transition elements like chromium prefer a 4s1 3d5 arrangement over 4s2 3d4, even though 4s is normally filled first.

q.q: An element has 3 naturally occurring isotopes with mass numbers 24, 25 and 26, present in the percentage abundance 79.0%, 10.0% and 11.0% respectively. Calculate the relative atomic mass of the element to one decimal place.
q.explanation: Relative atomic mass = (24 x 0.79) + (25 x 0.10) + (26 x 0.11) = 18.96 + 2.50 + 2.86 = 24.32, which rounds to 24.3. This weighted average method accounts for both mass number and abundance of each isotope.
